messages:
Maya (Support): :rotating_light: Getting a stack of escalations from APAC customers — multiple reports of SSE streams cutting off mid-response and clients doing tight reconnect loops. Biggest clusters: ap-northeast-1 and ap-southeast-1. Seeing this since ~2026-03-14T05:08Z.

Maya (Support): Symptoms: partial final chunks (last token truncated), connection stays open briefly then FIN, clients immediately reconnect, sometimes duplicate prefixes on reconnects. Some customers also report 401s after reconnects.

Kai (SRE): I'm seeing spikes in connection resets from our edge proxies in ap-northeast-1 at the same time window. Correlation with a proxy config push? Checking deploy history now.

deploy-bot: deploy event: edge-config/2026-03-14T05:03Z by infraops - rolled conf: http/keepalive/tcp_multiplex=true

Kai (SRE): That config matches the timing. Rolling back that edge change to disable multiplexing for APAC now.

Jin (Runtime Eng): Noted. Multiplexing can expose partial-frame buffering issues when combined with our chunked flush heuristic. If a proxy coalesces frames then the runtime's chunk boundary logic may drop the trailing small tail on abrupt disconnect. Need logs + sample request to reproduce.

Maya (Support): I have a customer repro. They used curl to stream:

```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=gpt-lite
```

They observed the stream cut after ~132 tokens with no final event. Attached request_id=apac:0a3f1c6b for one session.

Jin (Runtime Eng): Can you paste the server side tail of that request_id from logs? I want the socket-level events.

Maya (Support): Log excerpt:

```
2026-03-14T05:09:12.312Z request_id=apac:0a3f1c6b conn_id=42 edge=ap-northeast-1 PROXY_RESET: read 4096/4096
2026-03-14T05:09:12.313Z request_id=apac:0a3f1c6b runtime=session-7 flush_boundary=120 last_chunk_len=12 client_reconnect=true
2026-03-14T05:09:12.314Z request_id=apac:0a3f1c6b auth=ok token_ttl=60
```

Jin (Runtime Eng): Interesting — token_ttl=60s is short. Clients reconnecting quickly might be hitting token refresh races that return 401 on a reconnect path while the old connection is still tearing down. Two likely issues: proxy-level coalescing + short token TTL leading to auth flakiness on reconnect. Also the flush_boundary seems to be 120 which aligns with the partial chunk length.

Kai (SRE): Rollback completed for ap-northeast-1 and ap-southeast-1 (multiplex=false). Traffic should be rehomed to classic keepalive streams. Observability shows connection reset rate dropping to baseline in the last 2m.

Sophia (Customer Success): I'll send a short customer update. Suggest telling customers: we're investigating SSE interruptions in APAC, temporary mitigation: set client to exponential backoff on reconnect (>=500ms), or switch to non-streaming short-poll mode while we stabilize.

Sophia (Customer Success): Draft status blurb:

"We are investigating intermittent streaming interruptions for customers in APAC. We have rolled back a recent edge change and recommend customers set reconnection backoff and/or use polling (stream=false) as a temporary mitigation. We will provide updates within 30 minutes." :thumbsup:

statusbot: Incident created: APAC SSE partial-frames (INC-APAC-20260314-1) — investigating — https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-APAC-20260314-1

Kai (SRE): Short-term mitigations applied:
- rolled back edge multiplex config for APAC
- set proxy idle timeout to 90s (was 30s) to reduce mid-stream FINs
- enabled connection sticky routing so established sessions avoid re-proxying across AZs

Jin (Runtime Eng): Runtime fixes in flight:
- change flush heuristic to prefer flushing on explicit token-boundary markers
- make final-chunk ack resilient to probe resets (idempotent finalization)
- add more verbose socket debug for the suspected coalescing path

Jin (Runtime Eng): Patch branch pushed: github.com/redwood/runtime/PR-541. Requesting a quick canary in ap-southeast-1 for 5% traffic after the rollback is stable.

Kai (SRE): Canary scheduled at 2026-03-14T05:30Z. I'll watch RPS and connection reset metrics. If reset rate spikes > 2x baseline we'll rollback canary.

Maya (Support): Workarounds for customers we told them:
- Use polling: POST /v1/completions with stream=false
- Increase client reconnect backoff and jitter
- If they must stream, add a client-side finalization check: if stream reconnects, fetch final chunk via non-streaming call with same prompt and subtract tokens (avoid duplicates)

Maya (Support): Example polling curl:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-lite","prompt":"...","stream":false}'
```

Sophia (Customer Success): A couple of paying customers asked if we can route them to US-east as an emergency fallback. What's the feasibility?

Kai (SRE): We can route per-customer via routing-policies: set region_preference=us-east-1 for their API key. Doing that now for two customers that asked. Note: latency will increase ~150-250ms but stream integrity should be fine.

Jin (Runtime Eng): Also note fallback to a non-streaming model variant (same model family but a shorter seq policy) as a safety net if streaming remains unstable. Example: model=gpt-lite -> model=gpt-lite-stable (non-stream-optimized) via routing override.

Maya (Support): Two customers moved to us-east. Both reported resumed complete responses on test requests after switch.

statusbot: INC-APAC-20260314-1 update: mitigations deployed (edge rollback, proxy timeout), canary in progress. Next update in 20m or on status change.

Kai (SRE): Monitoring: connection resets back to baseline, token-refresh 401s have stopped after we increased auth token TTL to 5min for the APAC region (temporary). We'll revert TTL change after full fix.

Jin (Runtime Eng): Next steps:
- finalize runtime patch for flush heuristic (PR review in 2h)
- instrument finalization ack path and run 1h canary
- add regression test for proxy coalescing (unit + integration)

Sophia (Customer Success): I'll update customers with the note that we've applied temporary mitigations and are testing a runtime patch. Keep me posted on canary status.

Maya (Support): Closing loop on initial escalations: all open tickets in the thread were updated with mitigation steps and fallback instructions. Will escalate to engineering if we see reoccurrence after canary.

Kai (SRE): Thanks everyone. If the canary stays green at 05:45Z we schedule the runtime rollout for 06:15Z with a gradual 20/50/100% ramp.

Jin (Runtime Eng): I'll be online for rollout. If anyone sees partial frames again, capture request_id and attach tcpdump from the edge host and runtime debug logs.

Sophia (Customer Success): :heart: Great coordination. I'll post a customer-focused update in 10m.

Maya (Support): Thread note: for support agents — use the troubleshooting checklist: 1) check edge deploys in last 15m; 2) validate token TTL; 3) try routing override to us-east; 4) suggest polling as fallback. Paste checklist into internal KB.

Kai (SRE): Adding checklist to incidents KB and tagging INC-APAC-20260314-1.

statusbot: Incident update appended to INC-APAC-20260314-1 — mitigations effective, canary green.

Maya (Support): Marking this thread resolved for now. Will re-open if regressions reported.
